summary: New idiom: šqile/šoqəl u=mamro (mit mən-) ‘jemandem im Ratespiel das Wort entziehen’

data.headword: šqile/šoqəl u=mamro (mit mən-) ‘jemandem im Ratespiel das Wort entziehen’
data.turoyo: Bəṯr hənnək ste, am məštaʕyone, kul ḥa gdomalle xabro. Gdomər: “Be flan kas ne.” Haka qasimi, šxa gqəsmi w gšəqli u mamro mine.
data.translation: Dann sagt jeder von den Spielern etwas, z. b.: "Das ist die und die Familie." Wenn sie richtig raten, so raten sie eben richtig und entziehen ihm das Wort.

rationale: One game-specific turn-taking collocation; keep domain restriction rather than proposing a general speak sense.

summary: New idiom: šqile/šoqəl pežən d- ‘Nachricht von jemandem erhalten’

data.headword: šqile/šoqəl pežən d- ‘Nachricht von jemandem erhalten’
data.turoyo: Komər me d azzele w karəx aʕle, šqile pežən diḏe, mərre: "Kale b flan qriṯo."
data.translation: Als er ging und nach ihm suchte, bekam er Nachricht über ihn; man sagte: „Er ist in dem und dem Dorfe.“

rationale: Single clear location-news expression; sym pežən uses a different light verb.

summary: New idiom: šqile/šoqəl faġro ‘die Kommunion empfangen’ (cf. qurbono)

data.turoyo: Annaqla u zlamayḏan, Šamʕən, zlam mšiḥoyo yo, gud lo kul arbʕi yawme šoqəl faġro, lo kowe gabe, yaʕni bu qonuno di ʕitayḏan hawxa yo.
data.translation: Nun war unser Mann, Schamun, ein guter Christ, und bei uns geht es nicht an, daß ein Christ vierzig Tage verstreichen läßt, ohne den leih des Herrn zu empfangen; nach den Gesetzen unserer Kirche ist es so.

rationale: Sacramental-body variant of inherited communion idiom; no technical numbered sense.

summary: New idiom: šqile/šoqəl stəqlaliye, əstəqlaliye ‘Unabhängigkeit erlangen, verschaffen’

data.turoyo: <...> Slaq ftaḥ u Ṭuro, mḥay bu Ṭuro w šqal stəqlaliye <...>
data.translation: <...> Go up, open up the mountain country, fight in the mountain country and take independence. <...>

rationale: Political collocation, supported independently at Jan 1160 and 1403; beneficiary -lan at 1403. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: New idiom: šqile/šoqəl tadbir ‘Maßnahmen, Vorsichtsmaßnahmen treffen’

data.turoyo: <...> Bəṯr i ḥkume šqila tadbir lə qadər Ḥaǧo oṯe. <...>
data.translation: <...> Afterwards the government took measures; Hajjo could not come. <...>

rationale: Same administrative collocation at Jan 342 and 1843; group rather than number it as a lexical sense. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: New idiom: šqile/šoqəl nəqṭo ‘einen Punkt erzielen’ (cf. puwane [R1])

data.turoyo: <...> Xəd u naqwo, u ḥa d mḥaləq, d moyəd i čamme d mḥalaqla bi qalʕo d mqabəl. Šuqalwo nəqṭo, šuqalwo puwan.
data.translation: <...> Like the hole, the one who throws, who brings the little stick to throw it into the opposite goal, would take a point, would take a point.

rationale: Literal game scoring variant nəqṭo; puwan in parallel supports round-1 puwane rather than a new numbered technical sense. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: New idiom: šqile/šoqəl ǧaṣara ‘Mut fassen’

data.turoyo: <...> Lə ṭuretu d ḥəzyo aṣ ṣəroye lašan d lə šəqlo ǧaṣara. Mḥawtekunne! <...>
data.translation: <...> Do not let her see the Christians, so that she does not take courage. Drive them away! <...>

rationale: One clear courage-taking collocation in a negative purpose clause; no numbered sense. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: New idiom: šqile/šoqəl qarar ‘einen Beschluss fassen’

data.turoyo: <...> Bəṯər lu Sənnados di ʕito šqiwole qarar, səmwole šabṯo mi xaṣrayo w šabṯo mayo. Yaʕni šabṯo bu rišo w šabṯo bi ḥarayto. <...>
data.translation: <...> Afterwards the Church Synod had taken a decision; they had made it a week on this side and a week on that side. That is, a week at the beginning and a week at the end. <...>

rationale: Institution makes its own ruling; distinguish inherited qarār obtaining another person’s opinion and hyw 1 giving a ruling. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: New idiom: šqile/šoqəl qopya ‘eine Kopie nehmen, eine Darstellung übernehmen’

data.headword: šqile/šoqəl qopya ‘eine Kopie nehmen, eine Darstellung übernehmen’
data.turoyo: <...> Han naqqa mawxa Yusəf Saʕid šəqlole qopya mərole haṯe (gaḥxo).
data.translation: <...> Then Yusef Said took a copy from here and told this (laughing).

rationale: One qopya collocation with subsequent telling mərole; physical copying versus repeating an account remains open. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: New idiom: šqile/šoqəl quro ‘sich erkälten’

data.turoyo: <...> Hawxa šqili quro, mḏ̣ayaʕali ruḥi, l uḏaʕnowo, ayko no. Hawxa ḥəmme gawonayto kəmmila. Msəkla i lašayḏi kula. <...>
data.translation: <...> I had caught cold like this; it made me lose myself. I did not know where I was. An internal fever like this, they call it. It seized my whole body. <...>

rationale: One clear cold-taking collocation, supported by fever and bodily illness in Turoyo. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: New idiom: šqile/šoqəl rəxṣa, daṣtur ‘Erlaubnis einholen’ (cf. musaʕada [R1])

data.turoyo: Yaʕni lə nǧəḥle d šoqəl rəxṣa. <...>
data.translation: That is, he did not succeed in taking permission. <...>

rationale: Permission noun variants at Jan 3550/3552; converse of hyw 1 giving permission, not a duplicate. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: New idiom: šqile/šoqəl dars (mit mən-) ‘eine Lehre ziehen’

data.turoyo: <...> D məftakər, d šuqele dars, čike maḥ ḥaye du qadišo yo, d əzzeyo li ʕito, haṯe yo.
data.translation: <...> So that he reflects, so that he should take a lesson from a little of the saint's life, so that he should go to church; that is it.

rationale: Single clear lesson-taking collocation with source maḥ ḥaye du qadišo; do not infer a general study sense. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: New idiom: šqile/šoqəl taqdir ‘Anerkennung finden’

data.turoyo: Uʕdo, zaṭan aʕ ʕitawoṯayḏan kšuqli taqdir b ʕayne dan awruppawiye, kuḏʕət mən yo?
data.translation: Now our churches receive appreciation in the eyes of the Europeans, do you know what that is?

rationale: Three related church-appreciation statements; the appreciation noun supplies the predication, so keep under Idiomatic phrases. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: Taking the soul covers literal death-taking and figurative exhaustion; JTM 3.2/23 and 4.4/2 support the inherited ruḥo idiom's figurative branch.
Recorded objects include voices, stories and songs; material variation does not create new senses.
Animals can be the agents of the established i=raḥa rest collocation.
Weeds can deprive grain of strength (i humma mu zad): abstract resource and plant participants, not a new lexical sense.
Literal property loss with l aloho šqile meni (43/40) must be distinguished from the formally similar loss-of-reason idiom.
The distance collocation accepts a filly as agent; retain the edition's motion rendering without making leaping an independent meaning of šql.
Jan confirms round-1 bride-arranger construction, including its previously empty Infectum-wa cell; collective family participation at 219 does not automatically require the arranger-only analysis.
Literal game scoring with puwan confirms round-1 puwane; nəqṭo is its explicit point-noun variant.
The inherited hawa and raḥa expressions recur; ventilation subject at 299 remains uncertain and no new numbered sense is published.

Themes extend to buildings, rescued persons, results, names, qualifications, information, thought, happiness and political control. Documents include daskara (identity/discharge) and tarxis; these do not establish purchase or independent discharge senses.
Legal collectors, including an overt l-marked female judge at 1024, take ifada. This supports the inherited expression and round-1 agent analysis.
Permission-taking and opinion-gathering are productive nominal frames; musaʕada and opinion acquisition were already treated in round 1, while permission noun variants are indexed here.
Further R2 evidence for loss of possession, inspiration received from scriptural study and a plural political participant noun. These do not establish separate acquisition senses.
Bank pension-drawing supports round-1 monetary receipt/collection sense; the habitual šoqalwayno context does not create a new sense or missing Infectum box.
